items.stem: Which term is defined as "a small circle of DNA found in bacteria, separate from the main chromosome"?
items.answer: Plasmid
items.markingKey: Plasmid: a small circle of DNA found in bacteria, separate from the main chromosome.

items.stem: Explain why bread dough rises when left in a warm place.
items.answer: Yeast respires anaerobically, producing carbon dioxide; bubbles of gas are trapped in the dough, so it expands; warmth increases enzyme activity.
items.markingKey: CO₂ from yeast respiration [1]; bubbles trapped [1]; warmth increases rate [1] [3]

items.stem: Explain why biofuels are described as more sustainable than fossil fuels.
items.answer: The crops can be regrown each year, and the CO₂ released when they burn was taken in by photosynthesis while they grew.

items.stem: Lucas put equal masses of bread dough containing yeast into measuring cylinders, kept them in water baths at different temperatures and measured the increase in volume after 30 minutes. Results table. Temperature / °C: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. Increase in volume / cm³, trial 1: 1, 9, 39, 45, 28; trial 2: 1, 9, 39, 49, 18; trial 3: 1, 9, 37, 48, 19. Describe a suitable control for this investigation and explain why it is needed.
items.answer: Dough made with boiled (dead) yeast — any change in volume would not be due to yeast respiration.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: control described; 1 mark: shows that the change is caused by the independent variable [2]

items.stem: Diego put equal masses of bread dough containing yeast into measuring cylinders, kept them in water baths at different temperatures and measured the increase in volume after 30 minutes. Results table. Temperature / °C: 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. Increase in volume / cm³, trial 1: 9, 38, 47, 18, 2; trial 2: 9, 53, 48, 18, 2; trial 3: 9, 36, 47, 19, 2. (a) State two variables that should be kept constant in this investigation. (b) Suggest one way to improve this investigation.
items.answer: (a) Mass of dough; mass of yeast and sugar in the dough. (b) Press the dough to the bottom of the cylinder so the starting level is flat.
items.markingKey: (a) Any two from: mass of dough; mass of yeast and sugar in the dough; time; diameter of measuring cylinder; type of flour [2] (b) Any one from: press the dough to the bottom of the cylinder so the starting level is flat; use a thermometer to check the temperature inside the dough; repeat each test more times and calculate a mean (to improve reliability); test more values of the temperature (smaller intervals), especially near the turning point / extremes [1]

items.stem: Nadia put equal masses of bread dough containing yeast into measuring cylinders, kept them in water baths at different temperatures and measured the increase in volume after 30 minutes. Results table. Temperature / °C: 15, 25, 35, 45, 55. Increase in volume / cm³, trial 1: 3, 20, 47, 32, 7; trial 2: 2, 20, 47, 34, 7; trial 3: 3, 21, 44, 33, 7. (a) Calculate the mean increase in volume at 15 °C, ignoring any anomalous result. (b) State the type of graph you would draw to display these results and what you would plot on each axis.
items.answer: (a) 3 cm³ (b) A line graph: temperature on the x-axis and mean increase in volume on the y-axis.
items.markingKey: (a) (3 + 3) ÷ 2 [1] = 3 cm³ [1] [2] (b) line graph (continuous independent variable) [1]; temperature on x-axis and increase in volume on y-axis [1] [2]

items.stem: Why are bacteria useful in biotechnology and genetic modification?
options: They have a nucleus with many chromosomes
They reproduce rapidly and can make complex molecules
They cannot be grown in fermenters
items.answer: They reproduce rapidly and can make complex molecules
items.markingKey: Bacteria have no ethical concerns over their use and contain plasmids.

items.stem: Explain one disadvantage of growing crops for biofuels.
items.answer: Land is used for fuel instead of food, raising food prices; forests may be cleared, reducing biodiversity.

items.stem: Using C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂, how many molecules of ethanol are made from 5 molecules of glucose?
items.markingKey: 1 glucose → 2 ethanol, so 5 → 10.

items.stem: A biofuel plant in Riyadh ferments sugar from sugar cane: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂ (Mr glucose 180, ethanol 46, CO₂ 44). (a) Calculate the maximum mass of ethanol made from 900 kg of glucose. (b) Calculate the mass of carbon dioxide released. (c) In practice only 85% of this ethanol is obtained. Calculate the actual mass. (d) Suggest why the yield is less than 100%.
items.answer: (a) 460 kg (b) 440 kg (c) 391 kg (d) some glucose is used by yeast for growth / aerobic respiration; ethanol kills yeast at high concentration.
items.markingKey: (a) 900 ÷ 180 × 2 × 46 [1] = 460 kg [1] (b) 440 kg [1] (c) 391 kg [1] (d) glucose used for growth / yeast killed [1] [5]

items.stem: A biofuel plant in Bangkok ferments sugar from sugar cane: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂ (Mr glucose 180, ethanol 46, CO₂ 44). (a) Calculate the maximum mass of ethanol made from 180 kg of glucose. (b) Calculate the mass of carbon dioxide released. (c) In practice only 90% of this ethanol is obtained. Calculate the actual mass. (d) Suggest why the yield is less than 100%.
items.answer: (a) 92 kg (b) 88 kg (c) 82.8 kg (d) some glucose is used by yeast for growth / aerobic respiration; ethanol kills yeast at high concentration.
items.markingKey: (a) 180 ÷ 180 × 2 × 46 [1] = 92 kg [1] (b) 88 kg [1] (c) 82.8 kg [1] (d) glucose used for growth / yeast killed [1] [5]

items.stem: What is the name for "a detergent containing enzymes such as proteases and lipases that digest stains"?
items.answer: Biological washing powder
items.markingKey: Biological washing powder: a detergent containing enzymes such as proteases and lipases that digest stains.

items.stem: Explain why biological washing powders should not be used in very hot water.
items.answer: High temperatures denature the enzymes, changing the shape of the active site so stains are not digested.
items.markingKey: denatured [1]; active site shape changed [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain how enzymes in biological washing powders remove stains.
items.answer: Proteases and lipases digest insoluble proteins and fats into small, soluble molecules that wash away in water.

items.stem: Sofia added pectinase to 50 g samples of chopped apple at different temperatures, left them for 15 minutes, then filtered each for 10 minutes and measured the volume of juice collected. Results table. Temperature / °C: 15, 25, 35, 45, 55. Volume of juice / cm³, trial 1: 6.5, 9.5, 20.8, 28, 20.1; trial 2: 6.5, 10, 19.7, 28.3, 11.8; trial 3: 6.1, 9.5, 20.4, 27.1, 20.7. Identify the anomalous result in the table and state what should be done with it.
items.answer: Trial 2 at 55 °C (11.8 cm³); it should be ignored when calculating the mean (or repeated).
items.markingKey: trial 2 at 55 °C identified [1]; ignore / repeat it [1] [2]

items.stem: Daniel added pectinase to 50 g samples of chopped apple at different temperatures, left them for 15 minutes, then filtered each for 10 minutes and measured the volume of juice collected. Results table. Temperature / °C: 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70. Volume of juice / cm³, trial 1: 6.8, 13.1, 22.5, 22.9, 13.3, 7.1; trial 2: 7, 7.8, 22.3, 23.1, 12.9, 7.4; trial 3: 7.4, 13.1, 22.3, 22.8, 12.4, 7.3. (a) Suggest one way to improve this investigation. (b) Calculate the percentage increase in juice volume from the lowest temperature to the optimum.
items.answer: (a) Bring the apple and enzyme to the test temperature before mixing. (b) 225%

items.stem: Arjun added pectinase to 50 g samples of chopped apple at different temperatures, left them for 15 minutes, then filtered each for 10 minutes and measured the volume of juice collected. Results table. Temperature / °C: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. Volume of juice / cm³, trial 1: 6.2, 7.2, 12.2, 21.6, 22.2, 12; trial 2: 5.8, 7.2, 11.9, 21.2, 21.4, 12.1; trial 3: 5.8, 7.2, 7.7, 21.8, 21.2, 12.7. (a) Identify the independent variable and the dependent variable in this investigation. (b) Describe a suitable control for this investigation and explain why it is needed.
items.answer: (a) Independent: temperature; dependent: volume of juice. (b) Apple with boiled (denatured) pectinase, or water instead of enzyme, at each temperature — shows how much juice is released without active enzyme.
items.markingKey: (a) independent variable = temperature [1]; dependent variable = volume of juice [1] [2] (b) 1 mark: control described; 1 mark: shows that the change is caused by the independent variable [2]

items.stem: Explain why the lactase used to make lactose-free milk is often immobilised on beads.
items.answer: It can be reused, does not contaminate the milk, and the milk can flow over it continuously.

items.stem: Explain why fruit juice treated with pectinase is clearer.
items.answer: Pectin and cell wall debris that make juice cloudy are broken down into soluble substances.

items.stem: A dairy in Toronto makes lactose-free milk. Milk contains 4.8 g lactose per 100 cm³. 1000 cm³ of milk is passed over immobilised lactase and 80% of the lactose is broken down. (a) Calculate the mass of lactose in 1000 cm³ of milk. (b) Calculate the mass of lactose remaining after treatment. (c) Name the products and describe a test to show that they are present.
items.answer: (a) 48 g (b) 9.6 g (c) glucose and galactose; glucose test strip / Benedict's test gives a colour change (more reducing sugar).

items.stem: Chloe placed squares of cloth stained with egg in biological washing powder solution at different temperatures and recorded the time taken for each stain to disappear. Results table. Temperature / °C: 10, 25, 40, 55, 70. Time for stain to disappear / min, trial 1: 26, 13, 8, 13, 57; trial 2: 40, 12, 8, 12, 57; trial 3: 29, 13, 7, 12, 54. (a) Describe the trend shown by the results. (b) Suggest one way to improve this investigation.
items.answer: (a) The time for stain to disappear decreases as the temperature rises to 40 °C, which gives the lowest value, then increases. (b) Use a colorimeter to judge when the stain has gone.
items.markingKey: (a) correct overall pattern [1]; data quoted with units / turning point given [1] [2] (b) Any one from: use a colorimeter to judge when the stain has gone; stir each sample at the same rate; repeat each test more times and calculate a mean (to improve reliability); test more values of the temperature (smaller intervals), especially near the turning point / extremes [1]

items.stem: Mateo added pectinase to 50 g samples of chopped apple at different temperatures, left them for 15 minutes, then filtered each for 10 minutes and measured the volume of juice collected. Results table. Temperature / °C: 15, 25, 35, 45, 55. Volume of juice / cm³, trial 1: 6.3, 9.2, 19, 28.4, 19.5; trial 2: 6.5, 9.2, 19.7, 26.7, 19.8; trial 3: 6.3, 9.7, 27.8, 28.6, 20.2. (a) State two variables that should be kept constant in this investigation. (b) Explain the results.
items.answer: (a) Mass of apple; volume and concentration of pectinase. (b) Pectinase breaks down pectin in cell walls, releasing juice; up to about 45 °C more kinetic energy gives more enzyme–substrate collisions; above the optimum the enzyme is denatured and the active site changes shape.
items.markingKey: (a) Any two from: mass of apple; volume and concentration of pectinase; time left before filtering; filtering time; size of apple pieces [2] (b) pectin broken down [1]; more collisions to optimum [1]; denaturation [1] [3]

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "batch culture"?
options: A method in which microorganisms are grown in a closed fermenter and the product is collected at the end.
A large vessel in which microorganisms are grown in controlled conditions to make a product.
An antibiotic produced by the fungus Penicillium.
The separation and purification of the product from a fermenter.
items.answer: A method in which microorganisms are grown in a closed fermenter and the product is collected at the end.
items.markingKey: Batch culture: a method in which microorganisms are grown in a closed fermenter and the product is collected at the end.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "a method in which microorganisms are grown in a closed fermenter and the product is collected at the end"?
items.answer: Batch culture
items.markingKey: Batch culture: a method in which microorganisms are grown in a closed fermenter and the product is collected at the end.

items.stem: Explain why the pH in a fermenter must be monitored and controlled.
items.answer: Enzymes in the microorganisms work best at an optimum pH; changes in pH (e.g. from CO₂ / waste) could denature enzymes and reduce growth and yield.

items.stem: What is the function of the waste gas outlet on a fermenter?
options: Keeps pH at the optimum for enzymes
Removes carbon dioxide produced by respiration
Keeps the temperature at the optimum for enzymes; respiration releases heat, so cooling water removes it
items.answer: Removes carbon dioxide produced by respiration
items.markingKey: Waste gas outlet: removes carbon dioxide produced by respiration.

items.stem: A pharmaceutical company in Singapore makes penicillin using the fungus Penicillium in a 100 000 dm³ fermenter kept at 30 °C and pH 6.5. Sterile air is bubbled through the culture, and cooling water flows through a jacket. (a) Explain why the air must be sterile. (b) Suggest why the company keeps the culture at 30 °C.
items.answer: (a) Unwanted microorganisms would contaminate the culture, compete for nutrients or produce harmful substances. (b) This is the optimum temperature for the enzymes of the microorganism, giving the fastest growth / highest yield.

items.stem: Explain why penicillin is collected after the fungus has stopped growing rapidly.
items.answer: Penicillium makes most penicillin when nutrients start to run out, after the main growth phase.

items.stem: A pharmaceutical company in Hanoi makes penicillin using the fungus Penicillium in a 100 000 dm³ fermenter kept at 26 °C and pH 6.5. Sterile air is bubbled through the culture, and cooling water flows through a jacket. (a) Explain why the fermenter needs a cooling jacket. (b) Describe how the penicillin is obtained after fermentation.
items.answer: (a) Respiration of the microorganisms releases heat; without cooling, the temperature would rise above the optimum and enzymes would be denatured. (b) The culture is filtered to remove cells, then the product is extracted and purified (downstream processing).

items.stem: A pharmaceutical company in Hanoi makes human insulin using genetically modified bacteria in a 100 000 dm³ fermenter kept at 37 °C and pH 6.5. Sterile air is bubbled through the culture, and cooling water flows through a jacket. (a) Explain why the fermenter needs a cooling jacket. (b) State the purpose of the stirring paddles. (c) Explain why a probe is used to monitor the pH.
items.answer: (a) Respiration of the microorganisms releases heat; without cooling, the temperature would rise above the optimum and enzymes would be denatured. (b) Mix nutrients, oxygen and microorganisms evenly; distribute heat. (c) Waste products such as CO₂ change the pH; acid or alkali is added to keep the optimum pH for enzymes.

items.stem: Which is the correct definition of the term "recombinant plasmid"?
options: Something, such as a plasmid or virus, used to carry a gene into another organism.
Changing the genetic material of an organism by removing, changing or inserting individual genes.
An enzyme that cuts DNA at a specific base sequence, leaving sticky ends.
A plasmid into which a gene from another organism has been inserted.
items.answer: A plasmid into which a gene from another organism has been inserted.
items.markingKey: Recombinant plasmid: a plasmid into which a gene from another organism has been inserted.

items.stem: Explain two advantages of GM crops that are resistant to insect pests.
items.answer: Higher yield because less damage; less insecticide sprayed, so less harm to other insects and lower cost.

items.stem: Explain two concerns about growing herbicide-resistant GM crops.
items.answer: Genes may spread to wild relatives by pollen, producing herbicide-resistant weeds; more herbicide may be used, reducing biodiversity; seeds are expensive.

items.stem: Which enzyme is used in this step of making human insulin by genetic modification: "The insulin gene is inserted into the plasmid"?
items.answer: DNA ligase
items.markingKey: The insulin gene is inserted into the plasmid and joined with DNA ligase.

items.stem: These steps in making human insulin using bacteria are in the wrong order: P the bacteria multiply in a fermenter and express the gene, making human insulin; Q a plasmid is cut open with the same restriction enzyme, leaving complementary sticky ends; R the insulin gene is inserted into the plasmid and joined with dna ligase; S the recombinant plasmid is inserted into a bacterium; T the human insulin gene is cut out of human dna using restriction enzymes. (a) Put the letters in the correct order. (b) Explain why bacteria can make a human protein.
items.answer: (a) T → Q → R → S → P (b) the genetic code is universal, so the bacterium translates the human gene into the same sequence of amino acids.
items.markingKey: (a) T Q R S P: all correct [2]; three in correct positions [1] (b) universal genetic code [1] [3]

items.stem: These steps in making human insulin using bacteria are in the wrong order: P the human insulin gene is cut out of human dna using restriction enzymes; Q the recombinant plasmid is inserted into a bacterium; R the bacteria multiply in a fermenter and express the gene, making human insulin; S the insulin gene is inserted into the plasmid and joined with dna ligase; T a plasmid is cut open with the same restriction enzyme, leaving complementary sticky ends. (a) Put the letters in the correct order. (b) Explain why bacteria can make a human protein.
items.answer: (a) P → T → S → Q → R (b) the genetic code is universal, so the bacterium translates the human gene into the same sequence of amino acids.
items.markingKey: (a) P T S Q R: all correct [2]; three in correct positions [1] (b) universal genetic code [1] [3]

items.stem: Scientists in Madrid have produced a GM cassava variety containing a bacterial gene that makes a toxin harmful to insect pests. Some local groups oppose growing it. (a) Explain two concerns that the local groups might have. (b) Compare genetic modification with selective breeding.
items.answer: (a) Gene could spread to wild plants by pollen; harm to non-pest insects (e.g. pollinators); pests evolve resistance; seed costs / dependence on companies; reduced biodiversity. (b) GM: specific gene, can cross species, fast; selective breeding: whole genome, same species, many generations.

items.stem: Scientists in Mexico City have produced a GM maize variety containing a bacterial gene that makes a toxin harmful to insect pests. Some local groups oppose growing it. (a) Describe how the bacterial gene could be inserted into the crop plant cells. (b) Explain how pests could become resistant to the toxin.
items.answer: (a) Cut the gene out with restriction enzymes; insert it into a vector (plasmid of a bacterium that infects plants) with ligase; the vector transfers the gene into plant cells, which are grown into plants. (b) A random mutation gives some pests resistance; they survive and reproduce, passing on the allele (natural selection).

items.stem: Which enzyme joins the human insulin gene into a plasmid?
items.answer: DNA ligase
items.markingKey: Ligase joins sugar–phosphate backbones.

items.stem: Explain why Golden Rice was developed.
items.answer: It was genetically modified to produce beta-carotene (vitamin A precursor) to reduce vitamin A deficiency in countries where rice is the staple food.

items.stem: Explain why bacteria are used as hosts for genes for human proteins.
items.answer: They reproduce rapidly; contain plasmids; few ethical concerns; can be grown in fermenters on a large scale.

items.stem: Farmers in Nairobi compared non-GM soya with GM soya that has insect resistance (Bt toxin). Yield: non-GM 1.83 t/ha, GM 2.51 t/ha. Insecticide sprayed: non-GM 4.8 kg/ha, GM 2.1 kg/ha. (a) Calculate the percentage increase in yield. (b) Calculate the percentage decrease in insecticide used. (c) Suggest one environmental benefit and one possible risk of growing the GM crop.
items.answer: (a) 37.2% (b) 56.2% (c) benefit: fewer non-pest insects killed / less pollution; risk: genes spread to wild plants by pollen, pests evolve resistance, reduced biodiversity.

items.stem: Farmers in Muscat compared non-GM soya with GM soya that has insect resistance (Bt toxin). Yield: non-GM 1.89 t/ha, GM 2.41 t/ha. Insecticide sprayed: non-GM 5.0 kg/ha, GM 2.5 kg/ha. (a) Calculate the percentage increase in yield. (b) Calculate the percentage decrease in insecticide used. (c) Suggest one environmental benefit and one possible risk of growing the GM crop.
items.answer: (a) 27.5% (b) 50% (c) benefit: fewer non-pest insects killed / less pollution; risk: genes spread to wild plants by pollen, pests evolve resistance, reduced biodiversity.

items.stem: Describe how bacteria can be genetically modified to produce human insulin.
items.answer: Insulin gene cut from human DNA with restriction enzyme (sticky ends); plasmid cut with same enzyme; gene inserted and joined with DNA ligase; recombinant plasmid taken up by bacteria; bacteria multiply in fermenter; insulin extracted and purified.
items.markingKey: restriction enzyme [1]; sticky ends / same enzyme on plasmid [1]; ligase [1]; plasmid into bacterium [1]; fermenter [1]; extraction [1] [6]

items.answer: (a) Gene could spread to wild plants by pollen; harm to non-pest insects (e.g. pollinators); pests evolve resistance; seed costs / dependence on companies; reduced biodiversity. (b) A random mutation gives some pests resistance; they survive and reproduce, passing on the allele (natural selection). (c) GM: specific gene, can cross species, fast; selective breeding: whole genome, same species, many generations.

items.stem: Which product of yeast respiration makes bread rise?
items.answer: Carbon dioxide
items.markingKey: CO₂ bubbles are trapped in the dough.

items.stem: Explain why yeast is grown in sugar solution without oxygen to produce ethanol.
items.answer: Without oxygen yeast respires anaerobically, producing ethanol; with oxygen it would respire aerobically producing CO₂ and water.

items.stem: In Brazil, maize is grown and fermented by yeast to make ethanol, which is mixed with petrol for cars. (a) Explain why the fermenter is kept free of oxygen. (b) If starch from maize is used, explain why an enzyme is added before fermentation.
items.answer: (a) So yeast respires anaerobically and produces ethanol, not carbon dioxide and water. (b) Amylase breaks down starch to sugars (maltose / glucose) that yeast can respire.

items.stem: Why does pectinase increase the volume of juice extracted from apples?
options: It breaks down pectin, so cell walls break down and release juice
It adds water to the fruit
items.answer: It breaks down pectin, so cell walls break down and release juice
items.markingKey: Pectin holds cells together; breaking it releases juice.

items.stem: Arjun says: "Lactase breaks lactose down into amino acids." Explain whether Arjun is correct.
items.answer: Lactase breaks lactose into glucose and galactose.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error / statement is incorrect; 1 mark: Lactase breaks lactose into glucose and galactose. [2]

The separation and purification of the product from a fermenter.
items.answer: The separation and purification of the product from a fermenter.

items.stem: Explain why stirring is necessary in a fermenter.
items.answer: Keeps nutrients, oxygen and microorganisms evenly mixed and spreads heat evenly.

items.stem: Isla writes in a revision note: "Eating GM food will change your genes." Identify the error and write a correct statement.

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Explain why Golden Rice was developed. (b) Explain two concerns about growing herbicide-resistant GM crops.
items.answer: (a) It was genetically modified to produce beta-carotene (vitamin A precursor) to reduce vitamin A deficiency in countries where rice is the staple food. (b) Genes may spread to wild relatives by pollen, producing herbicide-resistant weeds; more herbicide may be used, reducing biodiversity; seeds are expensive.

items.answer: (a) 12 (b) 20 480 000 (c) the plasmid with the insulin gene is copied and passed to both daughter cells in binary fission.

items.stem: What is the first step in producing human insulin from bacteria?
options: Grow the bacteria in a fermenter
Insert the plasmid into the bacterium
Cut the insulin gene out of human DNA with a restriction enzyme
Join the gene to the plasmid with ligase
items.answer: Cut the insulin gene out of human DNA with a restriction enzyme
items.markingKey: The gene must be isolated first.

items.stem: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of genetically modifying crops such as soya, maize and rice.
items.answer: Advantages: insect resistance (less insecticide, higher yield), herbicide resistance (easier weed control), improved nutrition (Golden Rice), drought tolerance. Disadvantages: gene transfer to wild species, reduced biodiversity, resistance in pests, cost of seed, possible health concerns.
items.markingKey: three advantages [3]; three disadvantages [3] [6]

items.stem: Which is the balanced equation for the production of ethanol by yeast?

items.stem: Samuel placed squares of cloth stained with egg in biological washing powder solution at different temperatures and recorded the time taken for each stain to disappear. Results table. Temperature / °C: 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. Time for stain to disappear / min, trial 1: 10, 10, 8, 10, 46; trial 2: 16, 10, 7, 10, 42; trial 3: 16, 10, 8, 10, 42. items.answer: (a) Independent: temperature; dependent: time for stain to disappear. (b) Protease digests the egg protein into soluble amino acids; it works fastest near its optimum (about 40 °C); at low temperatures there are fewer collisions and at high temperatures the enzyme is denatured, so the time is longer.

items.stem: Describe how the conditions in an industrial fermenter are controlled for the large-scale production of penicillin, and explain why each is controlled.
items.answer: Temperature (probe and water jacket) – optimum for enzymes, removes respiration heat; pH (probe, acid/alkali) – optimum; oxygen (sterile air) – aerobic respiration; nutrients – growth; stirring – mixing; aseptic (steam sterilisation) – prevent contamination; product extracted and purified.

items.stem: Scientists in Toronto have produced a GM rice variety containing a bacterial gene that makes a toxin harmful to insect pests. Some local groups oppose growing it. (a) Explain two advantages of growing this GM crop. (b) Explain how pests could become resistant to the toxin. (c) Compare genetic modification with selective breeding.
items.answer: (a) Higher yields because less pest damage; less insecticide needed, saving money and reducing harm to other insects / people. (b) A random mutation gives some pests resistance; they survive and reproduce, passing on the allele (natural selection). (c) GM: specific gene, can cross species, fast; selective breeding: whole genome, same species, many generations.
